title: procrank、showmap 与系统内存全局视图
key_conclusions: procrank should be used before single-process deep dives because it ranks system memory contributors by PSS/RSS/USS/SwapPss.
showmap and smaps explain where a selected process spends memory at the mapping level, including heap, anon, dalvik spaces, code, stack, ashmem, memfd, and shared libraries.
dumpsys meminfo is an Android bucket view, while showmap/smaps are Linux mapping views; reliable diagnosis combines both before choosing HPROF, heapprofd, fd, or graphics evidence.
Low-memory triage should move from system snapshot to process ranking, mapping attribution, owner evidence, and then same-scenario before/after validation.
shallow_points: The article does not include real procrank/showmap output from a device under pressure.
It does not validate procrank/showmap output differences across Android versions, userdebug versus user builds, or vendor ROMs.
It does not include a parser that joins procrank rows with showmap mapping deltas and dumpsys meminfo buckets.
It introduces dma-buf, ashmem, and memfd as mapping candidates but leaves ownership accounting for later topics.
